item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00251","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C13","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.9,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 plausibly supplied a material template for the child's explanation of the Panel's role. Both directives make collective bargaining and full use of ordinary conciliation and mediation the primary process, then provide a specialized board or panel for nationally important disputes that remain unresolved. The child adapts that machinery to atomic-energy labor relations and addresses the Panel's organizational placement. C13 has closely related policy language about party responsibility, voluntary settlement, mediation, and a supplemental fact-finding board, while C18 illustrates the machinery in operation, but neither matches the child's institutional logic as comprehensively as C21.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"place primary responsibility upon the parties to such disputes to make every effort to effect peaceful settlement through collective bargaining and the full use of mediation and conciliation","parent_excerpt":"preserve collective bargaining between labor and management ... any labor dispute which is not resolved by collective bargaining or by the prior full use of conciliation and mediation facilities","explanation":"Distinctive shared formulation establishes collective bargaining and ordinary mediation as prerequisites to special intervention."},{"child_excerpt":"special facilities available which may be used voluntarily to assist in arriving at peaceful adjustments of disputes which would imperil the program","parent_excerpt":"The parties to any such dispute jointly agree to submit such dispute to the Board for recommendation or decision ... or ... the dispute ... substantially threatens the progress of national defense","explanation":"Both create specialized dispute-settlement machinery combining voluntary use with a national-security predicate."},{"child_excerpt":"the Panel's special role as an aid to settlement only after the regular conciliation and mediation process has failed","parent_excerpt":"The Board may assume jurisdiction of any labor dispute which is not resolved by collective bargaining or by the prior full use of conciliation and mediation facilities","explanation":"The same sequencing and administrative role are stated almost directly: the special body acts only after normal bargaining and mediation fail."}]}
